-- **Fix:** the device is checked before anything runs. The iOS app (`boot_env` in `dm/ios/Sources/main.m`) does not start the host or the launcher on such a GPU: the screen says the device is not supported and names the GPU and the devices that are (iPhone 15 Pro or newer, M1 iPads or newer), and the log has a `[RED] boot:` line. `mtl_init` (`nvn_mtl.m`) stops every other route the same way, with a `FATAL … has no BC texture formats` line, for the NVN, Vulkan and GL layers alike; the classic-only path of a device without Metal 4 (a virtual Mac's shader capture) is left as it was.
+- **Fix:** the device is checked before the game starts. The iOS app checks it when Play is pressed (`front_ios_device_check` in `dm/ios/Sources/main.m`, called by `startGame` in `front_ios.m`, or at once in an app without a launcher) and does not start the host on such a GPU: the screen says the device is not supported and names the GPU and the devices that are (iPhone 15 Pro or newer, M1 iPads or newer), and the log has a `[RED] boot:` line. The check makes the process's first Metal device, and Metal reads `MTL_HUD_ENABLED` then, so it runs after the launcher has applied its settings; at launch (`boot_env`, before the launcher), it kept the launcher's **Performance HUD** switch from working ([GitHub issue #840](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/840)). The host's early loading, which makes no device, still starts at launch on such a GPU and is left unused. `mtl_init` (`nvn_mtl.m`) stops every other route the same way, with a `FATAL … has no BC texture formats` line, for the NVN, Vulkan and GL layers alike; the classic-only path of a device without Metal 4 (a virtual Mac's shader capture) is left as it was.

+  - **Learned pools:** the host maps each logged page to the memory pool holding it. The stores count as a write anywhere until the learned pools have stayed the same over 8 logs, then as writes over those pools. A later log that shows a page in another pool adds that pool, without going back to a write anywhere (only a log that ran out of slots starts the learning again): a write anywhere makes every later geometry draw of the submission wait for the GPU (`geo_cpu_hazard`), and going back for 8 logs after each miss gave Donkey Kong Bananza streaks of 300-2,000 ms frames (38 such frames in 5,400, 6 after the change, the geometry wait in one 25 s sample 3,490 → 264 ms). The host then checks whether the miss could have mattered: every uniform shadow taken from that submission on (its own and those of the later submissions encoded while it ran, each recorded with its fence) is compared with the pages the stores wrote outside the prediction. Only an overlap, or a record that has wrapped before the check, prints a `[RED]` line; a miss no shadow saw is logged with the pools' ages.
+- **Open:** the prediction is checked, not proven: a miss that does reach a shadow is reported (`[RED]`) after the frame, not prevented. The records' pointers come from memory, so the pools they will reach are not known ahead of the draw.
+- **Symptom:** `[RED] pipeline prewarm: seed list does not exist: …/pso_manifest.tsv` at every start, no `pipeline prewarm list …/pso_user.tsv` line, and the same compile stalls every session in places already visited, while `pso_user.tsv` keeps growing; the pipeline archive gains files every start and is never compacted (Donkey Kong Bananza: 88 files, 7 s to open them).

+- `nx_extract` stops with exit code 134 and `Unhandled exception. System.InvalidOperationException: The LinkedList is empty.` from `LibHac.Tools.FsSystem.CachedStorage.GetBlock`, with no `[RED] hash check failed` list, with or without `--allow-damaged`. → [Extraction of a damaged NSP ends in "The LinkedList is empty"](../reference/packing.md#extraction-of-a-damaged-nsp-ends-in-the-linkedlist-is-empty)

+- **Symptom:** `nx_extract` stops with exit code 134 and `Unhandled exception. System.InvalidOperationException: The LinkedList is empty.` from `LibHac.Tools.FsSystem.CachedStorage.GetBlock`, with no `[RED] hash check failed` list, with or without `--allow-damaged`.
+- **Fix:** the entry's last byte in a `DMROMFS1` index ([format](../../dm/tools/romfs_image.py)) is 1 on a file that failed the check (`img_ent.flags`, `romfs_image.h`; `nx_extract` sets it, and every reader refuses another value, or a flag on a directory). The mark stays with the image in an IPA, a Mac app or a hand-copied `romfs.img`. The host logs `[RED] fs RomFS image <path>: damaged files <N>: ...` at the mount and `[RED] fs rom:/<file> failed the NCA's hash check ...` at each damaged file's first open. A clean image is byte-identical to one from before this mark (checked on SteamWorld Dig), so its identity does not change. Not marked: an image extracted before this change, and folder extraction, which has no index (the NSP script writes images). Search a crash's log for `hash check` before looking for a cause in the host.
